White to slightly brownish powder (hydrochloride), slightly soluble in water.

Pregabalin: Developed as a more potent successor to gabapentin; pain relief may begin within the first week. First approval/introduction: Synthesised 1990 (Richard B. Silverman, Northwestern University); EU and US FDA 2004 (Pfizer).

Duloxetine: Created by Eli Lilly researchers including David Wong, co-inventor of fluoxetine; the (+)-S-enantiomer was selected for its greater serotonin reuptake inhibition. First approval/introduction: US FDA and EU 2004 (Eli Lilly and Company).
Pregabalin 75 mg + Duloxetine 20 mg (strength not stated in product list – common

Pregabalin reduces excitatory neurotransmitter release while duloxetine enhances descending inhibitory pain pathways – complementary mechanisms that allow lower doses of each, with improved pain relief (supported by the COMBO-DN study).

Pregabalin Binds the alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels with higher affinity than gabapentin, decreasing release of excitatory neurotransmitters; analgesic, anxiolytic and anticonvulsant. Receptor / target profile: Binds the alpha-2-delta-1 protein of voltage-gated calcium channels with high affinity, reducing release of glutamate, norepinephrine and substance P.

Duloxetine Potent inhibitor of neuronal serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake, weak dopamine reuptake inhibitor. Antidepressant effect and enhancement of descending inhibitory pain pathways underlie its use in depression, anxiety and chronic pain states. Receptor / target profile: Inhibits SERT (Ki 0.7–0.8 nM) and NET (Ki 7.5 nM) with negligible affinity for dopaminergic, cholinergic, histaminergic or adrenergic receptors.
Summary: Bioavailability ≥90% (linear); Tmax ~1 h. Not protein bound; negligible metabolism. Half-life ~6.3 h. Renally excreted unchanged – adjust dose to CrCl.
Summary: Delayed absorption (enteric-coated); Tmax ~6 h. >90% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP1A2 and CYP2D6. Half-life ~12 h.

Approved for GAD (7–17 y) and fibromyalgia (13–17 y) in some regions; monitor for suicidality and growth.

Pregabalin: Renal function; weight; oedema; misuse; respiratory status.
Duloxetine: Blood pressure; LFTs if symptoms; sodium in elderly; mood/suicidality early in treatment.

Pregabalin: Somnolence, confusion, agitation, restlessness, seizures (rare), coma. Supportive care; haemodialysis effective. Duloxetine: Somnolence, serotonin syndrome, seizures, vomiting, tachycardia. Supportive care; activated charcoal.
COMBO-DN (Tesfaye et al., Pain 2013) – combination of duloxetine and pregabalin was well tolerated in DPNP non-responders.
OPTION-DM (Tesfaye et al., Lancet 2022) – combination therapy improved pain when monotherapy was insufficient.
Dizziness, drowsiness and weight gain may occur
Swallow whole – do not crush or open
Do not stop suddenly – dizziness, irritability may occur
Report worsening mood or suicidal thoughts
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
